title: TrustBound: A Mechanized Note on Payment-Epoch Completeness
abstract: TrustBound studies payment completeness for AI-assisted travel booking. We formalize when a trusted payment service can account for every in-scope payment effect and establish that outstanding authority cannot produce further effects. Travel agents submit requests to the service without access to its credentials, journal, or administration. Our Lean admission model records each payment identity before granting authority. An admission fence then fixes the journal, which covers all modeled effects and outstanding rights. Once those rights are discharged, no later effect can occur in the model. Truthful reports for each journaled identity then give exact identity-level accounting. Our constrained provider-contract model requires registration before activation and keeps unregistered objects inert. The artifact checks 14 exported results; eight premise-removal mutations fail the proof checks. A finite evidence diagnostic shows how matching reports can still leave an effect unaccounted for. The note applies established closure principles under an explicit payment trust contract, with checked models and reproducible examples.
